Series::tracks_slope¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::tracks_slope() const -> bool

What It Does¶

tracks_slope() reports whether this Series is currently marked to participate in reverse-mode tracking.

If the answer is true, future differentiable computations that use this series can treat it as a tracked source and later populate sensitivity onto it when reverse() is called downstream.

If the answer is false, the series can still be used in forward computation normally, but reverse-mode will not store sensitivity onto it as a tracked leaf.

This is a state-inspection method. It does not change tracking behavior by itself. For mutation, use tracks_slope_().

Conceptually, this answers a setup question, not a differentiation question.

  • tracks_slope() asks: “if reverse-mode reaches this value later, should a sensitivity be stored here?”

  • reverse() asks: “given the finished forward result, what sensitivities should propagate backward?”

  • sensitivity() asks: “what sensitivity is currently stored on this series right now?”

Those three stages belong to one workflow, but they are not interchangeable.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

bool true when the Series is configured for reverse-mode tracking, otherwise false.

Examples¶

Example 1. A fresh Series is not tracked by default.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
std::cout << "before=" << (x.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

So ordinary construction gives you a normal numeric Series, not a tracked autodiff leaf.

Output¶

before=false

Example 2. The no-argument mutator enables tracking, and disabling flips the state back again.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
std::cout << "before=" << (x.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
x.tracks_slope_();
std::cout << "after_enable_default=" << (x.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
x.tracks_slope_(false);
std::cout << "after_disable=" << (x.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Notice that this is only configuration state. No derivative has been computed yet, and no stored sensitivity exists merely because the flag became true.

Output¶

before=false
after_enable_default=true
after_disable=false

Example 3. Tracking state and stored sensitivity are related, but not the same thing.

auto x = pluss::make_series({9.0, 10.0}, pluss::cfg::tracks_slope());
x.mul(4.0).sum().reverse();
x.clear();

std::cout << "tracks=" << (x.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "has_dL_dx=" << (x.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

So tracks_slope() staying true does not imply a stored sensitivity is currently present.

Output¶

tracks=true
has_dL_dx=false

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • tracks_slope() is configuration state, not proof that any reverse pass ran.

  • tracks_slope() == true does not imply has_sensitivity() == true.

  • A series can participate in forward computation normally even when this is false; the difference shows up when reverse-mode storage is expected.

Summary¶

Use tracks_slope() to inspect whether a Series is currently configured to receive reverse-mode sensitivity as a tracked value.

See Also¶

  • Series::tracks_slope_: mutate the tracking state.

  • Series::has_sensitivity: inspect stored sensitivity presence.

  • Series::reverse: propagate sensitivity to tracked leaves.
